_comment: Hand-authored extras merged onto rules by scripts/build-rules.ts. tldr powers 'Explain simply', keywords feed the natural-language search pass, actions become the Quick Actions row. Keyed by rule id.

mounted-combat.tldr: You can ride a creature one size larger than you. If it's trained you control it, but a controlled mount only gets to Dash, Disengage or Dodge on its turn. Mounting costs half your movement.
mounted-combat.example: A Medium fighter rides a Large warhorse. Climbing on costs 15 of their 30 ft of movement. On the fighter's turn the horse moves with them and can Dash; the fighter still gets their own full action to attack.

actions.label: Mount / dismount
actions.text: Mounting or dismounting costs movement equal to half your speed. You can't do it if you have 0 movement left.

falling.tldr: You take 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 feet fallen, capped at 20d6, and you land prone.
falling.example: Falling 40 feet is 4d6 damage — and you're prone when you land, so getting up costs half your movement next turn.

prone.tldr: Prone means you can only crawl (or stand up, which costs half your speed). You attack at disadvantage; melee attackers get advantage on you, ranged attackers get disadvantage.
prone.example: A prone goblin is easier to stab than to shoot: the fighter next to it has advantage, the ranger 60 ft away has disadvantage.

actions.label: Cost to stand
actions.text: Standing up costs movement equal to half your speed — 15 ft for a speed of 30.

opportunity-attack.tldr: When a creature you can see leaves your reach, you can spend your reaction to make one melee attack against it. Disengaging, teleporting, or being moved against its will doesn't trigger it.
opportunity-attack.example: The goblin steps from 5 ft to 15 ft away — you get one swing. If it had Disengaged first, you get nothing.

grappling.tldr: Replace one attack with a Strength (Athletics) check against the target's Athletics or Acrobatics. Win and its speed drops to 0. You need a free hand and a target no more than one size larger.
grappling.example: A fighter with Extra Attack swings once, then grapples with the second attack instead of swinging again.

shoving-a-creature.tldr: Replace one attack with a Strength (Athletics) check against the target's Athletics or Acrobatics. Win and you either knock it prone or push it 5 feet.
shoving-a-creature.example: Shove the ogre prone, then every melee ally attacking it this round has advantage.

concentration.tldr: One concentration spell at a time. Take damage and you make a Constitution save — DC 10, or half the damage taken if that's higher — or the spell ends.
concentration.example: Hold Person is up and you take 26 damage. The DC is 13 (half of 26), not 10.

death-saving-throws.tldr: At 0 HP you roll a d20 at the start of each turn. 10 or higher is a success, under 10 a failure. Three successes stabilises you, three failures kills you. A natural 20 puts you back up at 1 HP; a natural 1 counts as two failures.
death-saving-throws.example: Taking any damage while down is an automatic failure — two if the hit was a critical.

critical-hits.tldr: A natural 20 always hits and is a critical: roll the attack's damage dice twice, then add your modifiers once.
critical-hits.example: A greatsword crit is 4d6 + Str, not 2d6 doubled including the modifier.

advantage-and-disadvantage.tldr: Roll two d20s and take the higher (advantage) or lower (disadvantage). They never stack, and having both at once cancels out to a single normal roll.
advantage-and-disadvantage.example: Three sources of advantage and one of disadvantage? You roll one plain d20.

cover.tldr: Half cover gives +2 AC and Dex saves, three-quarters gives +5, and total cover means you can't be targeted at all.
cover.example: An archer behind a low wall has half cover: AC 15 becomes effectively 17 against your shot.

jumping.tldr: With a 10-foot run-up, you long jump your Strength score in feet and high jump 3 + your Str modifier. Without the run-up, halve it. The distance comes out of your movement.
jumping.example: Str 16 with a run-up clears a 16-foot gap; standing still, 8 feet.

surprise.tldr: If you didn't notice the threat, you're surprised: no move, action or reaction on your first turn, and attacks against you have advantage until that turn ends.
surprise.example: The rogue's Stealth beat the guard's passive Perception, so the guard is surprised — it loses its whole first turn.

initiative.tldr: Everyone rolls a Dexterity check at the start of combat. Highest goes first.

hit-points-and-damage.tldr: Damage comes off your current HP. At 0 you drop unconscious and start rolling death saves — unless a single hit's leftover damage matches your HP maximum, which kills you instantly.

temporary-hit-points.tldr: Temp HP is a buffer that absorbs damage first. It never stacks — take the bigger number — and it can't be healed.

healing.tldr: Healing can't take you above your maximum, and any single point of healing brings a dying creature back to consciousness.

exhaustion.tldr: Six stacking levels, each worse than the last: disadvantage on checks, half speed, disadvantage on attacks and saves, half HP maximum, speed 0, then death. A long rest removes one level.

long-rest.tldr: Eight hours, at most an hour of it light activity. You get all your HP back, half your Hit Dice, and shed one level of exhaustion. Once per 24 hours.

short-rest.tldr: An hour of downtime. You can spend Hit Dice to heal — roll the die and add your Constitution modifier for each one spent.

two-weapon-fighting.tldr: Attack with a light weapon in one hand, then use your bonus action to attack with a different light weapon in the other. The off-hand attack adds no ability modifier to damage.

underwater-combat.tldr: Melee attacks are at disadvantage without a swim speed, unless you're using a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear or trident. Most ranged weapons miss automatically past normal range.

ranged-attacks-in-melee.tldr: Firing a ranged weapon with a hostile creature within 5 feet of you gives you disadvantage.

difficult-terrain.tldr: Every foot costs two — so difficult terrain halves how far you actually get.

movement-and-speed.tldr: You can split your movement around your action however you like, but you can't end your turn in another creature's space.

actions-in-combat.tldr: Each turn you get one action, your movement, and one reaction you can use on anyone's turn. Bonus actions only exist when a feature grants one.

reactions.tldr: One reaction per round, refreshed at the start of your turn. Using it doesn't cost your action or movement.

ready-action.tldr: Spend your action to set a trigger and a response. When the trigger fires you spend your reaction to act. Unused, it's lost at the start of your next turn.

dodge.tldr: Attacks against you have disadvantage and you make Dex saves with advantage, until your next turn. You lose it if you're incapacitated or your speed drops to 0.

armor-class.tldr: AC is the number an attack roll has to meet or beat to hit you.

attack-rolls.tldr: d20 + ability modifier + proficiency (if proficient) against the target's AC. Natural 1 always misses, natural 20 always hits.

saving-throws.tldr: d20 + the relevant ability modifier, plus proficiency if you're proficient in that save. A spell's DC is 8 + the caster's spellcasting modifier + their proficiency.

ability-checks.tldr: d20 + ability modifier, plus proficiency if the skill applies, against a DC the DM sets.

passive-checks.tldr: A passive score is just 10 + your modifiers — used when nobody's actively looking, most often passive Perception against someone's Stealth.

vision-and-light.tldr: Dim light means disadvantage on sight-based Perception. Darkness blinds you outright. Darkvision turns darkness into dim light, in greyscale, out to its range.

carrying-capacity.tldr: You can carry your Strength score × 15 pounds before anything slows you down.

inspiration.tldr: Spend it for advantage on one roll. You either have it or you don't — it never stacks.

flanking.tldr: Flanking is an optional rule that isn't on by default. Where a table uses it, standing opposite an ally gives advantage on melee attacks — check with your DM first.

spell-slots.tldr: Casting a leveled spell burns a slot of that level or higher; casting with a bigger slot often scales the effect. Slots come back on a long rest.

rituals.tldr: A ritual spell can be cast 10 minutes slower to avoid spending a slot, if your class allows ritual casting.

casting-time.tldr: Most spells take an action. If you cast one with a bonus action, the only other spell you can cast that turn is a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action.

spell-components.tldr: V needs your voice, S needs a free hand, M needs the component (or a focus, unless the spell lists a cost).

combining-spell-effects.tldr: The same spell cast twice doesn't stack; different spells do.

instant-death.tldr: If the damage that drops you to 0 has leftover damage equal to or greater than your HP maximum, you die on the spot.

stabilizing-a-creature.tldr: A DC 10 Medicine check or a healer's kit stops the death saves. The creature stays unconscious at 0 HP until it gets actual healing.

unconscious.tldr: You're incapacitated, prone, and drop what you're holding. Attacks against you have advantage, and any hit from within 5 feet is a critical.

grappled.tldr: Your speed is 0. It ends if the grappler is incapacitated or something moves you out of reach.

restrained.tldr: Speed 0, disadvantage on attacks and Dex saves, and attackers have advantage on you.

paralyzed.tldr: Incapacitated and unable to move or speak, you fail Str and Dex saves automatically, and every hit from within 5 feet is a critical.

stunned.tldr: Incapacitated, can't move, barely able to speak; you auto-fail Str and Dex saves and attackers have advantage.

frightened.tldr: Disadvantage on attacks and checks while you can see the source, and you can't move any closer to it.

charmed.tldr: You can't attack or target the charmer with harmful effects, and it has advantage on social checks against you.

poisoned.tldr: Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

blinded.tldr: You auto-fail anything needing sight, attack at disadvantage, and attackers have advantage on you.

invisible.tldr: You attack with advantage and attacks against you have disadvantage — but noise and tracks can still give you away.

petrified.tldr: Turned to stone: incapacitated, unaware, resistant to all damage, and auto-failing Str and Dex saves.

deafened.tldr: You can't hear, and auto-fail anything that needs hearing.
